description:
src/methods/mod.rs:74-78 — `updated`, `not_updated`, and `not_destroyed` are `HashMap<String, …>`. RFC 8620 §5.3 specifies these are maps keyed by Id (server-assigned object identifier). `created` and `not_created` are correctly String-keyed because they use caller-supplied creation keys, but the other three should be `HashMap<Id, …>`.

Wire-format consequence today: harmless because `Id` is `#[serde(transparent)]` over `String`, so deserialization succeeds. API consequence: callers who pull a key out of `set_response.updated` get a `String` and cannot use it interchangeably with the `Id` they get from `destroyed` or from any `/get` response. Forces `Id::from(s)` round-trip at every consumer.

Cross-crate note: identical shape in jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:77,80,82. Both crates were written together. Filing here for the calendars crate; mail-client should be matched.

Caveat: jmap-mail-client and jmap-base-client are LOCKED. Coordinating this would require a session-bound API change. Possibly worth deferring but worth recording.
title: SetResponse keys typed as String, RFC 8620 says they are Ids
